title: Absolute Error and MAE
outcome: By the end, I can explain absolute error and mae using a traced example and a stated limitation.
scenario: Compare absolute and squared error without losing track of units.
given: Residuals are [-1, 2, 3] cm. Use MAE=mean absolute residual and MSE=mean squared residual.
All inputs and outcomes in this worked example are invented classroom data; no real model run is claimed.

steps.label: Squared errors
steps.detail: Squares1, 4, 9 give MSE14/3 cm², approximately = 4.67 cm².

explanation: Read the picture in order. RMSE=sqrt(14/3), approximately2.16 cm. The arrows show which recorded input or intermediate result each decision uses. Explain the deciding step aloud before checking the changed case; pointing to the final answer alone does not show how it follows.

counterfactual.prediction: MAE becomes20 mm; MSE becomes1400/3 mm²; RMSE becomes about21.60 mm.
counterfactual.reason: Residuals scale by10; squares scale by100, while the square root returns a length unit.

student_task: Why is quoting MSE as4.67 cm misleading? Point to the relevant step in the picture, then write the changed result and the rule or evidence that supports it.
teacher_answer: Its unit is cm², not cm. RMSE is the corresponding square-root statistic with cm units. Changed-case check: MAE becomes20 mm; MSE becomes1400/3 mm²; RMSE becomes about21.60 mm. Residuals scale by10; squares scale by100, while the square root returns a length unit.
project_evidence: For your Responsible Plant Classifier, save the input, procedure, observed result and limitation of this check. Label this worked example as practice; use a different, previously unreviewed case when checking independent understanding.
limits: Different loss functions weight large misses differently; a smaller selected loss is not automatically better for every consequence.
review_note: Reviewed Absolute Error and MAE against the assigned lesson pack and its reserved independent case. Added a different explicit worked scenario, an auditable trace and a changed-input check; preserved the original curriculum and assessment boundary.
